content: The text provided is a detailed and highly technical dataset, primarily focused on studies related to the diagnosis and management of genital ulcer disease (GUD) and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). 1. A study conducted in the Dominican Republic (1995-1996) involved 81 male patients from a general practice setting. Clinical diagnosis of herpes was performed based on physical examination and patient history. Molecular PCR (M-PCR) testing identified 22 true positives, 11 false negatives, 66 false positives, and 43 true negatives. 2. In Peru (1995-1996), 63 male patients from general practice were evaluated for herpes using clinical diagnosis and M-PCR. The results showed 15 true positives, 12 false negatives, 17 false positives, and 19 true negatives. 3. A study in China (1998-1999) recruited 96 patients (52% male) from a sexual health clinic. Clinical diagnosis combined with M-PCR testing revealed 25 true positives, 8 false negatives, 36 false positives, and 27 true negatives. 4. Another study in China (2000-2001) included 227 patients (90% male) from a sexual health clinic. Clinical diagnosis, supported by M-PCR and darkfield microscopy, identified 49 true positives, 22 false negatives, 78 false positives, and 78 true negatives. 5. In Kenya (1980), 70 male patients from a special treatment clinic were assessed for syphilis using clinical diagnosis and culture methods. The results showed 33 true positives, 1 false negative, and 63 true negatives. 6. A South African study (year unclear) involved 210 male patients from a hospital setting. Clinical diagnosis, supported by culture, identified 52 true positives, 21 false negatives, 182 false positives, and 160 true negatives. 7. A systematic review of seven studies provided ten pooled estimates for detecting herpes from genital ulcers. Clinical diagnosis was based on physical examination and patient history, with diagnostic accuracy varying across studies. 8. In South Africa (2007), 642 patients (50% male) from a sexual health clinic were evaluated for GUD symptoms and risk factors. HSV-2 antibody testing identified 140 true positives, 347 false negatives, 22 false positives, and 133 true negatives. 9. A Kenyan study (2007-2009) enrolled 786 HIV-positive female patients from a general population study. Clinical diagnosis and HSV-2 IgG testing revealed 0 true positives, 14 false negatives, 14 false positives, and 796 true negatives. 10. In El Salvador (2008), 366 male patients living with HIV were assessed using self-reported symptoms and HSV-2 serology. The results showed 61 true positives, 262 false negatives, 5 false positives, and 38 true negatives. 11. Another El Salvador study (2008) focused on female sex workers (FSWs) and men who have sex with men (MSM). Among FSWs, HSV-2 serology identified 55 true positives, 7 false negatives, 234 false positives, and 69 true negatives. Among MSM, the results were 20 true positives, 64 false negatives, 234 false positives, and 69 true negatives. 12. A study in Madagascar (1997) recruited 196 patients (71% male) from a sexual health clinic. Clinical diagnosis and M-PCR testing identified 52 true positives, 4 false negatives, 112 false positives, and 28 true negatives. 13. In Jamaica (1996), 304 patients (83% male) from a sexual health clinic were evaluated. Clinical diagnosis and M-PCR testing revealed 21 true positives, 10 false negatives, 24 false positives, and 249 true negatives. 14. A Thai study (1995-1996) included 38 female sex workers from a sexual health clinic. Clinical diagnosis and M-PCR testing identified 0 true positives, 1 false negative, 11 false positives, and 36 true negatives. 15. In India (2011-2012), 96 male patients from a hospital were assessed for syphilis using clinical diagnosis, VDRL, and TPHA. The results showed 19 true positives, 24 false negatives, 1 false positive, and 52 true negatives. 16. A Rwandan study (1990-1992) involved 395 patients (63% male) from general practice. Clinical diagnosis, supported by RPR, TPHA, and darkfield microscopy, identified 108 true positives, 2 false negatives, 279 false positives, and 6 true negatives. 17. In the USA (1990-1992), 220 male patients from a sexual health clinic were evaluated using clinical diagnosis and darkfield microscopy. The results showed 14 true positives, 31 false negatives, 3 false positives, and 172 true negatives. 18. A Zambian study (1996) included 95 male patients from a hospital. Clinical diagnosis, supported by darkfield microscopy, RPR, and TPHA, identified 24 true positives, 17 false negatives, 14 false positives, and 40 true negatives. 19. In Lesotho (1993-1994), 92 patients from a sexual health clinic were assessed using clinical diagnosis and M-PCR. The results showed 54 true positives, 2 false negatives, 22 false positives, and 14 true negatives. 20. A Kenyan study (1990-1991) recruited 172 patients (47% male) from primary care. Clinical diagnosis and RPR testing identified 6 true positives, 18 false negatives, 19 false positives, and 129 true negatives. 21. In India (2008-2009), 181 male patients from a sexual health clinic were evaluated using clinical diagnosis and M-PCR. The results showed 26 true positives, 18 false negatives, 72 false positives, and 78 true negatives. 22. A systematic review of 13 studies provided 18 pooled estimates for detecting chancroid using clinical diagnosis. However, meta-analysis was not possible due to the limited number of studies. 23. A study in Rwanda (1994) involved 42 women and 38 men from health centers and hospital dispensaries. Among women, 34 cases of syphilis were identified. Among men, 37 cases of syphilis were diagnosed. 24. In South Africa (2000-2001), 587 patients from an STI clinic were evaluated. HSV was detected in 48% of cases, syphilis in 14%, and chancroid in 10%. 25. A Brazilian study (1995) included 156 patients from an STI clinic. Syphilis was diagnosed in 31% of cases. 26. In Zimbabwe (2015), 70 patients from clinics were assessed. HSV was detected in 17 cases, syphilis in 8 cases, and LGV in 1 case. 27. A Malawian study (1992-1993) involved 778 patients from an STI clinic. Chancroid was detected in 204 cases, and syphilis in 137 cases. 28. In the USA (1994), 516 patients from STI clinics were evaluated. HSV was detected in 320 cases, syphilis in 51 cases, and chancroid in 16 cases. 29. A systematic review highlighted the rarity of explicit evaluations of WHO algorithms for syndromic management of GUD.
